clue.text: Ride in which first part is shorter than second

definitions.text: Ride in which first part is shorter than second

parts.words: Ride in which first part is shorter than second
parts.note: a fairground ride whose name splits into two halves, playfully described as if one half were the shorter leg of a journey

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trip whose opening leg is briefer than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of a journey's stages, but the 'ride' is the fairground merry-go-round, and the 'parts' are the two halves of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round at a fair is also called by this name in Britain, a ride that circles endlessly.

clue.text: Dreadful man in charge of accommodation remains

definitions.note: plural noun in the clue, while the solution is singular, a leftover piece

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the word for a housing charge

parts.note: rent is the charge paid for accommodation

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so the next word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frightful landlord is left holding what's left.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap or residue is what remains after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Not far from nude — the way one gets half-baked

indicators.note: a near arrangement: the letters of the next word in a closely shuffled order

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone almost naked is told how one ends up half-baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not far from' signals NUDE with its letters shuffled to UNDE; the surface picture is sunbathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Food not cooked through is half-baked, insufficiently done.

clue.text: Occasion to remember pre-war alliance

parts.note: the alliance is a marriage made before the war, sixty years earlier, now celebrated as an anniversary

explanation.surface: A commemoration of a treaty signed before the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alliance' suggests a diplomatic pact; it is a marriage, and 'pre-war' (in 1997) puts it sixty years back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixtieth anniversary of marriage is the celebration named after a precious gem.

clue.text: Poison developing in food, having dished out pound in container

indicators.note: the jumbled letters and abbreviation sit inside the word for a container

parts.note: a bin is a container

indicators.note: dished means spoilt or ruined, so the letters of the next word are messed up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A toxin grows in food after someone served a pound of it in a tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished out' looks like serving food; 'dished' (ruined) is the anagram signal for the next word, and 'in' puts that plus L inside the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial toxin produced in badly preserved food causes botulism.

clue.text: Left to enter a French port without cargo

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left goes into the combined letters of the other two pieces

parts.note: un is French for a
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship leaving to enter a French harbour carries nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French port' suggests Calais or Le Havre; it is UN (French for 'a') then ADEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that is not loaded carries no freight.

clue.text: Doctor's left to clean up the bed-that's the limit!

indicators.note: the doctor has left, so his abbreviation departs from the word for scouring a river bed

parts.note: to dredge is to scoop silt out of a river or harbour bed
Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A physician has gone off, leaving someone to tidy the bed, which is the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bed' suggests a sickbed beside the doctor, but it is a river bed being dredged.
explanation.definitionFit: The rim or border of something marks its limit, the point beyond which it stops.

clue.text: Horse that's more thirsty

definitions.meaning: a clothes horse, a frame for drying washing
comparative of dry, as in thirsty

explanation.surface: A racehorse that is thirstier than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is a clothes horse, a frame for airing washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse dries laundry, so is an appliance for drying; feeling dry means feeling thirsty.

clue.text: Sight I witnessed while listening

indicators.note: heard by a listener, so the words are said aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: I saw, which in a British accent sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A witness recounts what they saw while eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the R is silent, so 'I saw' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A sight' colloquially means something ugly to look at.

clue.text: It wraps up charge in case

definitions.text: It wraps up charge in case

parts.words: It wraps up charge in case
parts.note: thick paper once used to wrap a gunpowder charge into a casing for a firearm

explanation.surface: Something packaged in case of a fee being levied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' and 'in case' read as a fee and a precaution; they are the gunpowder charge and the round's casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy rough paper was originally made for rolling ammunition rounds, and now serves for drawing.

clue.text: They help to make one informed, I assume

definitions.text: They help to make one informed, I assume

indicators.note: the letters of the closing words help make up the answer, which is tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A speaker hedges about what keeps people well informed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines press and broadcasting, while the run across 'informed, I assume' contains the answer; 'help to make' points to the letters sitting inside that run.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, broadcasting and similar outlets collectively keep the public informed about events.

clue.text: Take vital parts with long speeches?

indicators.note: parted or broken up, so the letters of the two preceding words are split and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the essential sections from something wordy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun after 'vital', but it is a verb signalling that TAKE VITAL is broken up and rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chatters at length is inclined to talk a great deal; the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Like the engine of a motor-bike — or its rider

definitions.text: Like the engine of a motor-bike
definitions.meaning: many motorcycle engines are kept at a safe temperature by finned cylinders exposed to the passing breeze rather than water
the rider, too, is chilled by the rushing wind

explanation.surface: A comparison between a motorcycle's engine and the person astride it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the finned engine and the exposed biker have their temperature lowered by the moving atmosphere around them.

clue.text: Bodywork?

parts.note: read as a work of art showing a body: a sculpture of the trunk alone

explanation.surface: A one-word query about car panels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodywork' suggests a car repair shop; here it is a sculptor's work depicting a human trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue of the human trunk without head or limbs is a classic sculptural form.

clue.text: Walked, after short time, with staff to study

parts.note: T is the usual abbreviation for time
a rod is a stick or staff
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: Someone took a walk after a brief pause, carrying a stick to their study.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod, past tense of tread, means walked; this is its participle form, as in 'has walked'.

clue.text: Simplicity of original native quarter

indicators.note: inventive or novel, so the letters of the next word are set in a new order

parts.note: E, East, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: The unspoilt simplicity of an indigenous district of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native quarter' reads as a district of a colonial city; NATIVE is rearranged and E is a compass quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless innocence or unworldliness is a kind of simplicity.

clue.text: Get rid of careless air cadet before start of exam

indicators.note: the cadet's words are carelessly thrown together, so their letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Remove a sloppy young trainee before an exam begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or eliminate something completely is to get rid of it.

clue.text: Hand over for the time being

definitions.meaning: to give something formally to someone, as a prize
at this moment, as in 'at the moment' or currently

explanation.surface: Give something up, just temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a gift formally is to bestow it; the time now, between past and future, is the current moment.

clue.text: From which a deduction may be made before loss

definitions.text: From which a deduction may be made

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a miss is a failure or loss

explanation.surface: A tax deduction before a financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deduction' suggests subtraction; it is logical inference. This spelling is a recognised variant of premise.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition from which a conclusion is drawn is the starting point of an argument.

clue.text: After this rite, one goes bare headed into church

definitions.text: After this rite, one goes bare headed into church

parts.words: After this rite, one goes bare headed into church
parts.note: a ceremony shaving the crown of a monk's head on admission to holy orders, leaving it literally bare

explanation.surface: A worshipper removes their hat before entering church after a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bare headed' looks like taking off a hat; here the head is shaved on joining the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving part of the scalp marks entry to monastic or clerical life.

clue.text: Characters producing singular sound as leaders of chorus, say

definitions.text: Characters producing singular sound as leaders of chorus, say

parts.words: Characters producing singular sound as leaders of chorus, say
parts.note: a pair of letters that together make one sound, as the opening two letters of the word chorus do

explanation.surface: Performers singing alone while leading a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' and 'chorus' suggest actors and singers; the characters are written letters, and the leaders of 'chorus' are its first two, C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-letter combination spelling a single phoneme, such as ph or ch, is a linguistic term.

clue.text: Extremely wet description of French quarter one's entered

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: the numeral one has gone into the compass quarter, splitting it

parts.note: west is one of the four quarters of the compass
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A description of a French district that someone has visited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French quarter' suggests New Orleans; 'entered' puts the numeral inside the compass quarter. 'description' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word describing something covered with morning moisture means the most damp.

clue.text: Came out of one's shell, having seen a change at the top

definitions.text: Came out of one's shell, having seen a change at the top

parts.words: Came out of one's shell, having seen a change at the top
parts.note: a chick breaking out of its egg, with the top of the shell giving way

explanation.surface: A shy person gains confidence after new management arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came out of one's shell' sounds like shyness overcome; it is literal for a chick leaving its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird emerging from its egg is born from the shell.

clue.text: Revise boundary round Eastern state

indicators.note: the word for boundary goes round, enclosing the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: an end is a limit or boundary
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a state on the US east coast

explanation.surface: Someone redraws a border around a state in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text is to revise it.

clue.text: Daughter in dire need expired

indicators.note: the daughter's abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
dire means terrible, so the letters of the next word are in a bad way and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl in desperate want passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has expired has finished or come to a close.

clue.text: Novel race providing material for papers

parts.note: novel means new
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: A new kind of contest that supplies stories for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap paper stock on which newspapers are printed is the raw material for them.

clue.text: Popular impression you heard about binding agreement

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a dent is an impression in a surface

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for the listener sounds like a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun sounds like the letter U
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A popular impression that you have picked up concerning a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract binding an apprentice to a master is a formal agreement of service.

clue.text: Sing for stunning girl

definitions.meaning: slang for informing on accomplices to the police
an attractive young woman, a looker

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sing in honour of a beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' is underworld slang for turning informer, not making music.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on criminal associates is an old slang sense; a lovely person is praised as a fruit-like delight.

clue.text: Fountain whose waters sparkle

parts.note: a counter dispensing fizzy drinks in a café, rather than an ornamental fountain

explanation.surface: An ornamental fountain with glittering water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fountain' suggests a garden feature; it is the soft-drink counter, whose carbonated water fizzes.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated water is fizzy, sparkling water served from such a dispensing counter.

clue.text: Sort of stationery landlord at the Crown used

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is jokingly one who lets
the crown is the top of the head

explanation.surface: Writing paper printed for the publican of the Crown pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Crown' reads as a pub name; in Britain pubs are often called the Crown, but here crown is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper printed with a name and address at the top is a type of stationery.
